nodes.label: Industry Home Page
nodes.rationale: Single-scroll home page that stacks hero, featured projects, latest articles, videos, skills and contact so a visitor can assess the developer without leaving the page; deep pages exist only for the full lists.

nodes.label: Industry Design System (ds/industry.css)
nodes.rationale: All five pages import one stylesheet and drive every color, space and font through CSS custom properties (--color-accent-700, --space-8, --font-heading) instead of literal values, so the whole site can be re-skinned to another direction by swapping the ds/*.css file alone.

nodes.label: Blueprint Corner Motif
nodes.rationale: class="blueprint" plus four empty <i class="corner tl|tr|bl|br"> elements draw engineering-drawing crop marks on cards, figures and primary buttons; kept as decorative empty elements rather than pseudo-elements so all four corners can be positioned independently.

nodes.label: Duotone Image Treatment
nodes.rationale: Every image is wrapped in a .duotone container so heterogeneous user-supplied screenshots and portraits are forced into one steel-blue palette and the page stays visually coherent regardless of source imagery.

nodes.label: image-slot Placeholder Component
nodes.rationale: A custom element (image-slot.js) with id/shape/placeholder attributes stands in for real media so the layout can be reviewed at full fidelity before any asset exists; each slot carries a stable id (ind-portrait, prj-1, vid-1, art-hero) for later replacement.

nodes.label: Trilingual Language Switcher (EN/TR/AR)
nodes.rationale: EN/TR/AR anchors carry data-lang attributes and are duplicated in both nav and footer; the active language is signalled only by color (--color-accent-700 vs --color-neutral-600). Arabic implies an RTL requirement the current LTR-only layout does not yet address.

nodes.label: data-i18n Translation Binding
nodes.rationale: Translatable strings are marked with dotted data-i18n keys (nav.home, hero.viewProjects, contact.send) and swapped at runtime by i18n.js, keeping the static HTML as the English source of truth instead of maintaining one HTML file per locale. Coverage is partial: headings and labels are keyed while body copy and card titles are not.

nodes.label: Primary Site Navigation
nodes.rationale: Identical nav markup is copied into all five pages (brand, Home/Projects/Articles/Videos, language switcher, Download CV); the current page is marked by accent color only, and on index.html the brand is a plain span rather than a link because it is already home.

nodes.label: Shared Site Footer
nodes.rationale: Copyright line plus a second copy of the EN/TR/AR switcher, duplicated verbatim across every page so the language control is reachable after a long scroll.

nodes.label: Home Hero Section
nodes.rationale: Asymmetric 1fr/380px grid pairs a stack-kicker, uppercase 64px name and dual CTA (View projects / Contact me) with a blueprint-framed portrait, leading with the tech stack rather than a job title.

nodes.label: Featured Projects Section
nodes.rationale: Three-up card grid mirroring the first three cards of the Projects page, with an 'All projects' escape hatch; curated subset on home, full catalogue behind the link.

nodes.label: Latest Articles Section
nodes.rationale: Text-only article teasers (date/topic kicker, title, one-line excerpt) with no imagery, deliberately quieter than the project cards so projects stay the visual focus of the page.

nodes.label: Home Videos Section
nodes.rationale: Two blueprint-framed video placeholders sit beside the articles column in a 1fr/1fr split, presenting writing and video as equal-weight content streams.

nodes.label: Skills Section
nodes.rationale: Skills are grouped Backend / Frontend / Tools as tags, with tag-accent marking the headline technologies and tag-neutral the rest, avoiding percentage or star proficiency meters.

nodes.label: Contact Section
nodes.rationale: Offers both direct channels (email, GitHub, LinkedIn, YouTube, CV download) and an inline name/email/message form; the submit button is type="button" with no action, so the form is presentational until a backend or form service is wired up.

nodes.label: Java / Spring Boot / React Positioning
nodes.rationale: The site positions its owner as a backend-first developer: the hero kicker, the About paragraph, the accent-tagged skills and the project tech tags (Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Java, React, Kafka, Docker) all repeat one stack, and even the article template's code sample is Java.
